claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of Co-free FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by temperature- and rate-sensitive activation of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
The activation of slip and twinning in Co-free FeNiCrMn is mediated by its solidified microstructure.
Grain-boundary character and fine-scale compositional fluctuations promote a balance between strength and ductility by activating different deformation modes.
Conventionally solidified and homogenized FeNiCrMn may retain fine-scale compositional variations.
Grain-boundary characteristics, nanoscale compositional fluctuations, or precipitates influence dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Grain-boundary characteristics, nanoscale compositional fluctuations, or precipitates influence the propensity for deformation twinning in FeNiCrMn.
At lower strain rates, dislocation slip predominates in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At higher temperatures, dislocation slip predominates in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At higher strain rates, deformation twinning becomes dominant in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At lower temperatures, deformation twinning becomes dominant in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning under high-rate or low-temperature loading enhances strain hardening.
The transition between dislocation slip and twinning governs the overall dynamic performance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature will produce a measurable shift from slip-dominated to twinning-dominated deformation.
The predicted deformation-mode shift will be reflected in strain-hardening behavior and post-mortem deformation patterns.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to samples containing extrinsic defects or processed by severe plastic deformation or other methods that fundamentally alter the initial microstructure.
